## 1. The structural theorem

Let \(E:M_a\to M_b\) be a finite-dimensional quantum channel. On its joint output support, define
\[
\Omega_E=E(I_a),\qquad
T_E(X)=\Omega_E^{-1/2}E(X)\Omega_E^{-1/2}.
\]
The map \(T_E\) is unital and completely positive. Form
\[
\mathcal A_E=C^*(T_E(M_a)),
\qquad
\tau_E(Z)=\frac1a\operatorname{Tr}(\Omega_E Z).
\]

Here \(\tau_E\) is a faithful state; it need not be a trace.

For two channels with the same input, the following are equivalent:

1. Their RLD quadratic profiles agree for every finite untouched reference, every faithful input baseline and every traceless Hermitian tangent.
2. All ordered moments of their normalized output generators agree under their respective faithful states.
3. There is an input-labelled, state-preserving unital \(*\)-isomorphism
   \[
   \theta:\mathcal A_\Phi\longrightarrow\mathcal A_\Psi,
   \qquad
   \theta T_\Phi=T_\Psi,
   \qquad
   \tau_\Psi\theta=\tau_\Phi.
   \]
4. All their complete maximal-perspective profiles agree.

The last conclusion actually extends to continuous functional calculus on the relevant positive spectra. It is stronger than equality for one selected divergence.

### The greatest representative

Let \(\mathbb E_{\mathcal A}\) be the ordinary trace-preserving conditional expectation onto \(\mathcal A_E\), and put
\[
Z_E=\mathbb E_{\mathcal A}(\Omega_E).
\]
Define
\[
\boxed{\Gamma_E(X)=Z_E^{1/2}T_E(X)Z_E^{1/2}.}
\]

This is a physical channel. Indeed,
\[
\operatorname{Tr}\Gamma_E(X)
=\operatorname{Tr}Z_ET_E(X)
=\operatorname{Tr}\Omega_ET_E(X)
=\operatorname{Tr}X.
\]
Its normalized output map is again \(T_E\), and its faithful state agrees with \(\tau_E\) on the generated algebra. Consequently, \(\Gamma_E\) belongs to the same complete-profile class.

There is an explicit deterministic operation taking it back to \(E\):
\[
\boxed{
\mathcal R_E(Y)=
\Omega_E^{1/2}Z_E^{-1/2}
\mathbb E_{\mathcal A}(Y)
Z_E^{-1/2}\Omega_E^{1/2}.
}
\]
Complete positivity follows from the displayed composition, while
\[
\mathcal R_E^*(I)
=
Z_E^{-1/2}\mathbb E_{\mathcal A}(\Omega_E)Z_E^{-1/2}
=I.
\]
Thus \(\mathcal R_E\) is trace preserving and
\[
\mathcal R_E\Gamma_E=E.
\]

The map is the established Petz transpose operation. The role it plays here is to recover the original outputs from the **newly constructed lifted outputs** \(\Gamma_E(X)\). Those generally differ from the ordinary coarse-graine
